research_question: Do the Experiment 11 representation and calibration-boundary effects persist under temporal-block holdout, and is temperature-feature interference independent of subject baseline normalization?

prerequisites.feature_checkpoints: Reuse all 15 hash-validated Experiment 9 feature checkpoints without loading raw WESAD pickles.
prerequisites.fold_continuity: Reuse the Experiment 10 ten-training/four-external/one-test subject rotation.

design.temporal_definition: Hold out every window in one within-state temporal tertile as test data; calibration and held-out-subject normalization may use only the other two tertiles.

normalization_contract.method: Per-subject median centering and IQR-to-robust-standard-deviation scaling.
normalization_contract.training_statistics: Computed independently from each training subject's own windows.
normalization_contract.heldout_statistics: Computed from the held-out subject's two non-test temporal tertiles, with no test-window access.
normalization_contract.support_rule: Compared across the full calibration grid with lda_raw_all, normalized-all must improve mean accuracy by at least 0.10, reduce mean full-set frequency by at least 0.05, retain at least 0.88 mean coverage, reduce worst-subject mean coverage by no more than 0.10, and improve accuracy by at least 0.05 in every held-out temporal tertile.

order_statistic_contract.fact: At alpha=0.10, k=18 uses the largest calibration score and k=19 uses the second-largest score.
order_statistic_contract.arm_support_rule: For each representation, k=18 to k=19 must reduce overall full-set frequency by at least 0.03, retain at least 0.88 mean k=19 coverage, reduce worst subject-phase coverage by no more than 0.05, and reduce full-set frequency in every temporal holdout.

temperature_rival_contract.raw_support_rule: At k=19, removing temperature must improve mean S2/S4 accuracy by at least 0.10, reduce their mean robustness loss by at least 0.03, and reduce overall accuracy by no more than 0.03.
temperature_rival_contract.normalized_support_rule: Apply the identical rule after subject normalization.
temperature_rival_contract.independent_interference: Both raw and normalized support rules pass.
temperature_rival_contract.baseline_mediated_interference: The raw rule passes, the normalized rule fails, and the S2/S4 accuracy benefit of temperature removal shrinks by at least 0.05 after normalization.
temperature_rival_contract.otherwise: Temperature interference does not replicate under this temporal protocol.

readiness_surface_contract.support_rule: Subject normalization passes its general rule and either raw versus normalized representations disagree on order-statistic-boundary safety or their k=18-to-k=19 coverage/full-set changes differ by at least 0.05.
readiness_surface_contract.interpretation: Support indicates an interaction between calibration-count geometry and representation; it does not establish a universal discontinuity or literature novelty.

predeclared_subject_checks.S4_replication: Across the full grid, normalization improves S4 accuracy by at least 0.30, reduces its full-set frequency by at least 0.20, retains at least 0.80 coverage, and produces a positive accuracy change in every temporal holdout.
predeclared_subject_checks.S2_residual_failure: Normalization improves S2 accuracy by less than 0.10 or increases its full-set frequency by at least 0.10.

guardrails: This is internal temporal replication within the same WESAD recording session, not independent-dataset replication.
S2 and S4 are confirmatory targets declared from Experiment 11 before Experiment 12 outcomes.
Temporal tertiles are relative positions within each labeled state run, not separate visits or days.
Accuracy, coverage, prediction-set size, and full-set frequency must be interpreted jointly.
No literature novelty claim will be made.
